_schema.purpose: Machine-readable old-to-new table of plan section 6 (vendor_command_overhaul_plan.md): how each 1.1.6 opcode maps onto the paged commands of firmware 1.1.7, for host maintainers porting a client. Firmware 1.1.7 answers none of the old opcodes. scripts/gen_vendor_protocol.py --check keeps the commands catalog and every adapter target and use consistent with dspi_commands.json.
_schema.commands: Every paged command of plan section 5, keyed PAGE.NAME: page mnemonic, cmd number, dir (G read, S write with payload, GS both, S0 zero-length action), addr kind (contract tokens), get_len (bytes, 'var', or null when unknown), set [min, max]. build names a firmware build condition. These are the plan's numbers, checked against dspi_commands.json by scripts/gen_vendor_protocol.py --check (the SET bounds of a BULK command are its own and not compared).
_schema.opcodes: One record per 1.1.6 opcode, keyed by its REQ_ name without the prefix: code, old_dir (W OUT write, R IN read, WR write-as-read IN, W+R both), and 'out' and/or 'in' adapters for the USB directions 1.1.6 accepted. A missing direction means 1.1.6 never handled it. The adapters describe how a 1.1.6 request is reproduced on the paged commands.
_schema.adapter.direct: Same direction and payload. target PAGE.NAME, wValue becomes the address unless addr says otherwise. trunc cuts an OUT payload. bulk allows an OUT payload over 64 bytes.
_schema.adapter.act_value: Write-as-read whose wValue is the value: a SET at addr (default 0) whose payload is one byte built from value {shift, mask} by encode (u8 low byte, u8_sat saturating, bool). The reply is the status byte of the status family.
_schema.adapter.act_addr: Write-as-read whose wValue is an address: a zero-length SET at addr (default wValue). Reply as act_value.
_schema.adapter.act_packed: Write-as-read packing address and value in wValue: addr {shift, mask} and value {shift, mask} are split out, then as act_value.
_schema.adapter.split: wValue (shifted and masked by selector) picks a case, each a full adapter. default handles unlisted selectors; null means 1.1.6 refused them (IN raises STALL, OUT is swallowed).
_schema.adapter.custom: A request with no one-to-one rule, named by fn. uses lists every paged command it touches as PAGE.NAME:G or PAGE.NAME:S. Extra fields are its data (GET_STATUS fields maps each selector to a struct, type and byte offset).
_schema.addr: {const: n} or {shift, mask, add}: address = ((wValue >> shift) & mask) + add.
_schema.on_stall: IN only. When the paged GET STALLs with a result in codes, answer len bytes of fill instead, reproducing a documented 1.1.6 zero-fill. Default is to raise the STALL.
_schema.out_stall: OUT only. 'raise' means 1.1.6 STALLed a rejected write too. Default means 1.1.6 ACKed a rejected OUT write silently, where 1.1.7 STALLs it.
_schema.status: Status family of a write-as-read (status_families). On success the family's success byte. On a STALL, SYS.LAST_RESULT is read and its VC_* name maps through status_overrides, then the family's from_vc. An unmapped or unreadable result raises the STALL.
_schema.retired: No paged replacement exists. The adapter emulates the 1.1.6 answer.

source: Documentation/Features/vendor_command_overhaul_plan.md sections 5, 6 and 6.1; Documentation/commands.md and vendor_commands.c at fb9a254 for 1.1.6 behaviour

preset.doc: PRESET_* (config.h). 0x03 CRC and 0x04 FLASH_WRITE are completion results the 1.1.6 handlers never returned synchronously

ack1.doc: Acknowledge byte 0x01. 1.1.6 STALLed every refusal, so any STALL is raised

RTA_SET_CONFIG.note: 1.1.6 STALLed a rejected config, so this rejection is not swallowed

UPMIX_SET_CONFIG.note: 1.1.6 STALLed a wrong length (and every request on RP2040), so this rejection is not swallowed

UPMIX_SET_PARAM.note: 1.1.6 STALLed a short payload, an unknown index and every request on RP2040, so paged refusals are not swallowed

in.note: Selectors not listed answer 4 zero bytes, as 1.1.6 did in release builds. 64 and up were loop profiler counters in DSPI_LOOP_PROF builds and are not translated.

GET_ADAT_INPUT_PIN.note: RP2040 1.1.6 stored and returned the pin; the boot default 0xFF is the closest fill

SET_ADAT_INPUT_CLOCK_MODE.note: RP2040 1.1.6 accepted this (0x00) so presets round-trip; an RP2350-only target answers 0x03 there

GET_CORE1_CONFLICT.note: golden 1.1.6: wValue past the last output answered 0x00, undocumented, so it is not zero-filled

SET_ALL_PARAMS.note: 1.1.6 ACKed and ignored 64 bytes or fewer, STALLed any other length but 6136 at SETUP, and dropped a bad header after the ACK

SET_ALL_PARAMS_CHUNK.note: 1.1.6 STALLed an out-of-order chunk at SETUP, so this rejection is not swallowed

SIGGEN_SET_CONFIG.note: 1.1.6 STALLed a rejected config, so this rejection is not swallowed

SET_SPDIF_INPUT_ENABLE.note: 1.1.6 answered 0x00 for an enable of index 0; INPUT.SPDIF_RX_ENABLE addresses inputs 1-3 only
